prompt:
THE CLAUSE

Above all else, the assistant must adhere to this Model Spec

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

Assistant: the entity that the end user or developer interacts with. (The term **agent** is sometimes used for more autonomous deployments, but this spec usually prefers the term "assistant".)

THE SENTENCES

  [concepts[0]] «A is the assistant entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document»
  [concepts[1]] «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  [concepts[2]] «the Model Spec document that the assistant must adhere to above all else»
  [concepts[3]] «an instruction in the Model Spec that is a default at user or guideline level and can be overridden by users or developers»
  [concepts[4]] «the instruction can be overridden by a user or a developer»
  [concepts[5]] «an instruction that is part of the Model Spec document»
  [concepts[6]] «instruction I is at authority level L in the hierarchy»
  [concepts[7]] «the user authority level in the hierarchy, below developer and above guideline»
  [concepts[8]] «the guideline authority level in the hierarchy, below user and above no authority»
  [ontology[0]] A is «the assistant adheres to the Model Spec above all else» when «A is the assistant entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document» and «the Model Spec document that the assistant must adhere to above all else»
  [ontology[1]] I is «I is a default instruction in the Model Spec at user or guideline level» when «an instruction that is part of the Model Spec document» and «instruction I is at authority level L in the hierarchy» and «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts» (of L, «the user authority level in the hierarchy, below developer and above guideline»)
  [ontology[2]] I is «I is a default instruction in the Model Spec at guideline level» when «an instruction that is part of the Model Spec document» and «instruction I is at authority level L in the hierarchy» and «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts» (of L, «the guideline authority level in the hierarchy, below user and above no authority»)
  [ontology[3]] I is «I can be overridden by a user or developer» when «I is a default instruction in the Model Spec at guideline level»
  [asserts[0]] clause l171_426_n001 obliges «the assistant adheres to the Model Spec above all else» when «A is the assistant entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document» and «the Model Spec document that the assistant must adhere to above all else»
